title: More places to shop, one place to sell
summary: Shopify was built to work wherever people shop. Every connected AI agent brings merchants a new place to sell, gives shoppers an easier way to buy, and makes Shopify's network stronger.
body_markdown:
Every aisle in a physical store ends. There’s always a back wall, a fixed number of shelves, and a narrow band at eye level where most items get picked, which is why brands often pay a premium to be there. Online shopping made the aisle longer, but that eye-level shelf was still there. Most people only read the first handful of search results and choose from those.


When an AI agent does the shopping, that shelf stretches much further. An agent can look past the first few results, search across more than a billion products all over the world, and keep searching until it finds the right fit. That means brands that aren’t at eye level start getting found. Around 75% of AI-referred purchases on Shopify come from outside the[top 100 product categories.](https://www.shopify.com/news/entrepreneurs-outselling-mainstream)


But however far the aisle stretches, it still needs what commerce has always demanded. Shelves that stay organized, with accurate pricing and inventory, so that they’re easily discoverable. Personalized service tailored to the shopper’s needs and preferences. A checkout with no line. Shopify has spent 20 years building just that: a commerce operating system for online stores, retail counters, wholesale, and enterprise, as one connected system that gets stronger as it grows.


[AI channels](https://www.shopify.com/news/agentic-commerce-momentum) are the newest place that system shows up. An agent can browse, compare, and even complete the purchase on someone’s behalf, without that person ever visiting a storefront. And every AI agent that connects to Shopify makes Shopify’s network stronger for the merchants, buyers, and developers already on it.


## The more who join, the better it works


Shopify’s network has three sides. It connects millions of merchants, the hundreds of millions of buyers who shop with them, and the developers building new ways to bring them together. That network grows stronger every time anyone joins, because each side makes the network more valuable to the other two.


Fraud protection is a concrete example. On its own, a small shop rarely sees enough orders to spot a stolen card. On Shopify, a card flagged at one store is already known at the next, because anonymized signals from millions of businesses inform Shopify’s defenses. Every order makes the next one safer, for the merchant and the buyer. Shopify Payments prevents more than 12,000 high-risk payments *every minute* .


Network effects carry over to AI channels, too.[Every merchant who joins](https://www.shopify.com/news/fall-26-edition-merchant) adds to a catalog of more than a billion products that agents can search. Every shopper who connects their Shop account to their agent brings their preferences and a checkout experience they already trust through Shop Pay. And every developer who builds[a new agentic experience](https://www.shopify.com/news/fall-26-edition-developer) with Shopify’s commerce infrastructure gives merchants another place to sell, which brings even more merchants and shoppers to the network.


None of this works if Shopify is a closed system. So Shopify was built to be an open ecosystem, and that now extends to agentic tools.


## Putting agents to work for merchants


AI is the newest front door into commerce, and more shoppers are entering through it. Last quarter, AI-driven traffic to Shopify stores grew 2.6x year over year, and orders grew 3.3x.


Merchants now sell to two personas: the human, and the agent shopping on their behalf. Agents don’t shop the way people do. They need accurate, live data; a set of rules for completing a purchase; and a seamless way to receive information in whichever AI chat shoppers use. Shopify builds for all three.


[Shopify Catalog](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-shopify-catalog) is written for agents, giving them live, structured product data, so it knows a particular pair of brown suede boots is on sale for $120 and that four are left in a size nine. Shopify started building Catalog three years ago, before most people had heard of agentic commerce. Today, AI search running on Catalog converts at *twice* the rate of general AI search.


And as the rules for agentic shopping get written, Shopify makes sure merchants keep a seat at the table as[new protocols take shape](https://sierra.ai/blog/releasing-poppy) . Shopify and Google co-developed the[Universal Commerce Protocol](https://www.shopify.com/news/ai-commerce-at-scale) , a shared language for agentic shopping. With UCP, an AI agent that buys from a store follows the merchant’s own checkout logic around shipping, pickup, discounts, taxes, and duties. Meanwhile, integrations with[major AI partners](https://www.shopify.com/ca/agentic-storefronts) including ChatGPT, Google AI Mode and Gemini, Muse, and others, put Shopify’s merchants in front of shoppers through the AI channels they already use. AI channels are sending shoppers straight to product pages at 3x the rate of organic search, and shoppers are converting 64% more often.


Agents are also an on-ramp for aspiring entrepreneurs. Someone can describe a[business idea](http://youtube.com/watch?si=j2HrbgeVj4ovu-cL&v=vj1ClDypAdY&feature=youtu.be) to an AI agent, build their store inside the chat, and start selling when they’re ready. And once they’ve started, they gain all the[AI business tools](https://www.shopify.com/blog/how-to-start-and-run-a-shopify-store-with-ai-agents) they need to manage and grow their business using AI agents like Sidekick, ChatGPT, and more, with Shopify powering the commerce behind each one.


## The newest way to shop, a familiar way to buy


To a buyer, all of this infrastructure is invisible. As more people let agents shop for them, their priority is that the agent finds what they actually want, and that they have the ability to purchase it securely. Shopify meets both needs in one place with Shop and Shop Pay.


When a shopper connects their Shop account, Shop uses what it knows about them to personalize the results the agent sees. The account brings[Shop Pay](https://x.com/rohitmishra/status/2102916764514611330) , so shoppers stay in control of what their agent buys and can pay with saved details the agent never sees. And it connects to the Shop app, so they can track the order alongside everything else they’ve bought.


Today, more than 400 million shoppers worldwide already trust Shop and Shop Pay. For an independent merchant, trust is the hardest thing to earn, and a shopper who trusts the Shop Pay button passes on that trust to the merchant using it. In Q3, 49% of orders through Shop came from people buying from that merchant for the first time.


Whatever wallet or card is used, the purchase runs through the merchant’s own Shopify checkout and lands in their admin like any other order. The order is theirs, the relationship is theirs, and the next purchase is theirs to earn.


## Wherever shopping goes next, the network is there


For 20 years, Shopify has grown by building what merchants need today and what they’ll need next. First, it was an easier way for entrepreneurs to open an online store. Then, the tools to help them scale up. And eventually, a unified system that works for the biggest brands in the world.


Every headline about a new shopping agent is really a headline about a new place for buying and selling. The human part remains unchanged: merchants want to sell what they make, and shoppers want to find products they love. They all just need it to work, wherever it’s happening.
